demos.description: Many equal temperaments lack an interval near a just 3/2, but still contain many useful scales constructed by stacking one generating interval.
Moment of symmetry scales consist of large (L) and small (s) steps mixed as evenly as possible. They use nominals from J onwards and J is always aligned with the root frequency.
Modes are selected by specifying an explicit pattern or by using UDP notation.
demos.tune:
# "Lorkhanic" of "Smitonic"
MOS{LsLsLLs}
J K L M N O P j=

# "Kagrenacan" of "Smitonic"
# Measuring from the root J...
# two scale degrees are bright (i.e. wide),
# while four degrees are dark (i.e. narrow)
MOS{4L 3s 2|4}
J K L M N O P j=

demos.description: The ratio between the sizes of L and s steps is called hardness. It defaults to 2:1 i.e. "basic" hardness. You can either provide the scale pattern in terms of small integers or by specifying L:s after the fact.
More complex step ratios require commas between the steps.
MOS scales that have multiple identical periods per octave have less modes available.
Ampersand & (read "am") raises by one chroma (L - s), while at-sign @ (read "at") lowers by one chroma.
demos.tune:
MOS{2L 5s}
J J& K L M N@ N O P j=

MOS{2L 5s 3:1}
J Je J& K L M N@ Na N O P j=

demos.description: Diamond-mos pitches get their own ups and downs from the underlying equal temperament.
demos.tune:
# Minihard Trial implying 17edo
# L = 7\17
# s = 3\17
# & = L-s = 4\17
# e = &/2 = 2\17
# ^ = 1\17 (always one step)
# / = 5\17 (always five steps)
MOS{2L 1s 7:3}
J ^J Je ^Je J& /J vK K

demos.description: Hardness declarations are not reduced. 8:4 implies basic hardness but finer octave division.
MOS ups and lifts are customizable. Integers are interpreted as steps of the host edo.
MOS equave is set by enclosing it in angle brackets.

demos.tune:
# 9edf is acceptable for Carlos Alpha
# "Dionian" of hard "Saturnian"
MOS{2L3s<3/2> 2|2 3:1}
J K L M N j=

demos.description: You can move the same MOS mode to a different key...
demos.tune:
# "Erev" of "Machinoid"
MOS{5L 1s}
J K L M N O j=

# Same scale but 4\11 higher
# J becomes J& and K becomes K&
MOS{key = L}
L M N O j k l=

demos.description: ...or specify a new UDP mode altogether.
demos.tune:
# "Medicinal" of "Manual"
MOS{4L 1s 3|1}
J K L M N j=

# Switch to "Indical" mode on K
# M becomes M@
MOS{key = K 1|3}
K L M N j k=

demos.description: Custom key signatures are supported. A natural sign restores the unaltered nominal.
When the system runs out of nominals it starts over but prefixes everything with a J.
MOS scales tuned to just intonation have irrational hardness so you have to define the size of a step directly.
